Subject: Cost Compression and Pilot Scorecard — post-call recap

Hi Samir / Alicia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the concrete next steps so we’re all aligned. I’ve attached a lightweight pilot-cost-model.xlsx and our Redwood playbook PDF for reference.

Top pain points you reiterated:
- Peak inference spend on high-concurrency webhooks (latency SLOs 150–200ms) is squeezing product roadmap spend.
- Current vendor lock-in makes experiments costly; procurement wants a predictable TCO.
- A/B rollout risk: output quality regressions are a blocker for committing budget without safety nets.

Goals we scoped:
1) Validate a 30-day pilot that shows 30–40% per-token cost compression (batching + prefix caching + quantized variant) while keeping latency within your SLO window for 95th percentile.
2) Deliver a pilot scorecard with cost delta, latency delta, and quality delta (prompt set of ~250 canonical flows).
3) Define a commitment path (monthly reserved capacity) if pilot meets benchmarks.

Cost levers we proposed (high level):
- Continuous batching for background workloads (~20–35% savings estimated for your QPS profile).
- Prefix/KV caching for repeat conversational prefixes (savings scale with reuse).
- Quantized inference variant for non-critical paths (aggressive token-level cost reduction but small quality delta to measure).
- Routing policy: route non-SLA traffic to cheaper regions / fallback models.

Immediate asks / owners:
- Samir: share a 30-day anonymized token volume sample (hourly granularity if possible) and a short prioritized prompt list (<=250 prompts) — due by EOD Friday 3/16.
- Marissa: we’ll draft an entry-level SOW and pilot success guardrails (cost + quality thresholds).
- Ben: provide a short ROI sketch showing monthly run-rate at current vs. pilot settings, plus a commit discount tier outline.

Proposed next meeting: Wed 3/21 10:00–11:00 PT to review the token sample and the SOW draft. If that works for everyone I’ll send a calendar invite.

Attachments: pilot-cost-model.xlsx (sheets: assumptions, sensitivity, scenario-results), redwood-playbook.pdf (pilot checklist + eval template).

Best,
Jasmine Liu

Samir — quick note on the compression numbers and ROI framing. Appreciate the budget constraint callout; we’ll design the pilot to be hard-capped under $25k unless you sign a PO for extra runway.

Compression expectations (based on similar customers and your described traffic mix):
- Backend batch jobs: 35–45% token-cost reduction via larger batching + cache priming.
- Real-time webhooks: 15–25% typical if strict P95 latency targets apply — savings come mainly from prefix caching and light batching where acceptable.
- Quantized variant: additional 10–15% on cheaper model variant tests; we run quality regression checks on your prompt set.

ROI sketch (high level):
- Baseline monthly inference cost: $62k (your figure from call).
- Pilot scenario (mixed): estimated monthly cost ~ $40k (35% reduction) -> monthly savings $22k.
- If pilot validated and you move to reserved capacity with modest commit (3–6 month), incremental discounting could lower unit cost another 10–15% depending on commit size.

I’ve created a condensed sensitivity table in the attached pilot-cost-model.xlsx under sheet 'scenario-results' and left notes on what inputs we need from you to finalize. For anonymization, we can accept an hourly token heatmap (no user IDs) which is simpler for you to export.

Next steps from our side:
- Jasmine: will send SOW draft and invite for 3/21.
- Ben: will produce a 2-page ROI one-pager for the call.
- Samir: token heatmap export when ready.

Thanks —
